cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubic bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the opposite pubis at the pubic symphysis; joins ilium and ischium within the hip bone and contributes to the acetabulum.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, superior ramus, inferior ramus, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, pecten pubis and obturator groove.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Pectineus, adductor longus, adductor brevis, gracilis and part of adductor magnus attach to the pubis; rectus abdominis attaches near the pubic crest/symphysis.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Symphyseal surface faces medially; body lies anteriorly; superior ramus lies above the obturator foramen.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacrum

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with L5 superiorly, both ilia at the sacroiliac joints, and the coccyx inferiorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Sacral promontory, alae, anterior and posterior sacral foramina, median sacral crest, auricular surfaces, sacral canal and sacral hiatus.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Piriformis arises from the pelvic surface; gluteus maximus and multifidus attach posteriorly; pelvic floor muscles attach to the lower lateral sacrum.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Broad base superior, apex inferior; smooth concave pelvic surface anterior, rough crested surface posterior.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coccyx

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the sacrum at the sacrococcygeal joint; coccygeal segments may fuse.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Base, apex, coccygeal cornua and transverse processes of the first coccygeal segment.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Coccygeus, levator ani and gluteus maximus attach to the coccyx; the anococcygeal body attaches anteriorly.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Base faces superiorly toward the sacrum and the apex points inferiorly, usually curving anteriorly.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urinary bladder

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores urine and expels it during micturition.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Apex, body, fundus/base and neck; the internal surface includes the trigone.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the male, lies posterior to the pubic symphysis and anterior to the rectum; seminal vesicles and ampullae of the ductus deferens lie between bladder and rectum.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4) contract detrusor and promote voiding; sympathetic fibres from T11–L2 favour storage; somatic pudendal control acts on the external urethral sphincter.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Superior vesical arteries and usually inferior vesical arteries; veins drain to the vesical venous plexus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Apex of the bladder
cards.label: 4a

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4a

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Anterior end of the bladder, directed toward the pubic symphysis.
cards.label: 4a

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Connected to the umbilicus by the median umbilical ligament, a remnant of the urachus.
cards.label: 4a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urinary fundus
cards.label: 4b

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4b

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Posterior surface/base of the bladder, opposite the apex.
cards.label: 4b

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the male, related to the seminal vesicles and ampullae of the ductus deferens; the rectum lies further posteriorly.
cards.label: 4b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Muscular layer (tunica muscularis)
cards.label: 4c

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4c

cards.question: Composition
cards.answer: Interlacing smooth muscle bundles forming the detrusor muscle.
cards.label: 4c

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contracts during micturition to expel urine.
cards.label: 4c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mucous coat (tunica mucosa)
cards.label: 4d

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4d

cards.question: Epithelium
cards.answer: Transitional epithelium (urothelium).
cards.label: 4d

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Allows distension while maintaining a urine-impermeable barrier.
cards.label: 4d

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ureteral orifice
cards.label: 4e

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4e

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Paired openings at the posterolateral angles of the trigone.
cards.label: 4e

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Receive urine from the ureters; the oblique intramural ureter helps limit vesicoureteral reflux.
cards.label: 4e

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigone of the bladder
cards.label: 4f

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Urinary bladder.
cards.label: 4f

cards.question: Boundaries
cards.answer: Triangular area between the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice.
cards.label: 4f

cards.question: Features
cards.answer: Mucosa is smooth and firmly attached to underlying muscle, unlike the rugae of the distensible bladder wall.
cards.label: 4f

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important cystoscopic landmark; irritation of the trigone can contribute to urinary urgency and frequency.
cards.label: 4f

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Prostate

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces prostatic secretions that contribute to semen.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Inferior to the bladder, surrounding the proximal prostatic urethra.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Base contacts bladder neck; apex rests on the external urethral sphincter; rectum lies posteriorly, allowing digital rectal examination.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Mainly branches of inferior vesical artery, with contributions from middle rectal and internal pudendal arteries.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Primarily internal iliac and sacral lymph nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Prostatic part of the urethra

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through the prostate from the internal urethral orifice to the membranous urethra.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra; surrounded by prostatic tissue.

cards.question: Openings
cards.answer: Receives prostatic ducts and ejaculatory ducts.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: May be compressed by prostatic enlargement, contributing to bladder outlet obstruction.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Urethral crest
cards.label: 6a

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Longitudinal ridge on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra.
cards.label: 6a

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Contains the seminal colliculus; prostatic sinuses lie on either side.
cards.label: 6a

cards.question: Openings
cards.answer: Ejaculatory ducts open on the seminal colliculus; prostatic ducts open into the prostatic sinuses.
cards.label: 6a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Seminal vesicles

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Secrete fructose-rich, alkaline seminal fluid that contributes a large proportion of semen volume.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Posterior to the bladder and anterior to the rectum, superior to the prostate.

cards.question: Duct
cards.answer: Each seminal vesicle joins the ampulla of the ductus deferens to form an ejaculatory duct.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Branches of inferior vesical and middle rectal arteries.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Autonomic fibres from the inferior hypogastric plexus; sympathetic activity promotes emission.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ductus deferens

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends in the spermatic cord, passes through the inguinal canal, crosses the external iliac vessels, then runs along the lateral pelvic wall and posterior bladder before enlarging as the ampulla.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Passes superior to the ureter near the posterolateral bladder.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Sympathetic fibres from pelvic plexuses drive strong peristaltic contraction during emission.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ureter

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transports urine from renal pelvis to urinary bladder by peristalsis.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends retroperitoneally on psoas, crosses the pelvic brim near the iliac vessels, then runs on the lateral pelvic wall and enters the bladder obliquely.

cards.question: Constrictions
cards.answer: At the pelviureteric junction, crossing of the iliac vessels/pelvic brim, and vesicoureteric junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the male pelvis, passes inferior to the ductus deferens before entering the bladder.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Visceral afferents travel mainly with sympathetic fibres to T11–L2 spinal segments; pain may refer from loin to groin.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Corpus spongiosum

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Surrounds and supports the spongy urethra while remaining sufficiently pliable to maintain urethral patency during erection.

cards.question: Extent
cards.answer: Begins proximally as the bulb of the penis and expands distally to form the glans penis.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies in the ventral midline of the penis, inferior to the paired corpora cavernosa.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Branches of the internal pudendal artery, especially the artery of the bulb and urethral artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Penis

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Organ of copulation and conduit for urine through the urethra.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Root, body and glans.

cards.question: Erectile tissues
cards.answer: Paired corpora cavernosa dorsally and a single corpus spongiosum ventrally.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Internal pudendal branches include deep arteries of the penis, dorsal arteries and artery of the bulb; skin also receives external pudendal contributions.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Somatic sensation mainly via the dorsal nerve of the penis; autonomic cavernous nerves regulate erection.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Glans penis

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Distal expansion of the corpus spongiosum.

cards.question: Features
cards.answer: Forms the corona and neck and contains the external urethral orifice at its tip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Rich somatic sensory innervation, mainly via the dorsal nerve of the penis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External urethral orifice

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: At the tip of the glans penis.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: External opening through which urine and semen exit the urethra.

cards.question: Features
cards.answer: Narrowest and least distensible part of the male urethra.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischiocavernosus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Compresses the crus of the penis and helps maintain erection by reducing venous outflow.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of the perineal nerve from the pudendal nerve (S2–S4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial surface of the ischial tuberosity and ischiopubic ramus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Crus of the penis and adjacent tunica albuginea of the corpus cavernosum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Testis

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces spermatozoa and testosterone.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Within the scrotum, suspended by the spermatic cord.

cards.question: Coverings
cards.answer: Tunica vaginalis externally and tunica albuginea directly surrounding the testis.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Testicular artery from the abdominal aorta; venous drainage via the pampiniform plexus into the testicular veins.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes, reflecting the embryological origin of the testes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior end of testis
cards.label: 15a

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Testis.
cards.label: 15a

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Related to the head of the epididymis.
cards.label: 15a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior end of testis
cards.label: 15b

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Testis.
cards.label: 15b

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Related to the tail of the epididymis and the scrotal ligament inferiorly.
cards.label: 15b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Epididymis

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Site of sperm maturation, storage and transport.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Head, body and tail.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Applied to the posterolateral surface of the testis.

cards.question: Continuity
cards.answer: Efferent ductules enter the head; the tail continues as the ductus deferens.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Head of the epididymis
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Organ
cards.answer: Epididymis.
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: At the superior pole of the testis.
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Receives the efferent ductules from the rete testis.
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pampiniform plexus

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Network of veins in the spermatic cord draining the testis.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Veins converge superiorly to form the testicular vein.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Countercurrent heat exchange cools arterial blood entering the testis and helps maintain optimal temperature for spermatogenesis.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Right testicular vein drains to the IVC; left testicular vein drains to the left renal vein.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Dilatation forms a varicocele, more commonly on the left.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Testicular artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Abdominal aorta, typically below the renal arteries.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends retroperitoneally, passes through the deep inguinal ring and inguinal canal within the spermatic cord to the testis.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Testis and epididymis.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Closely associated with the pampiniform plexus in the spermatic cord.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cremaster muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Elevates the testis and spermatic cord; contributes to thermoregulation and the cremasteric reflex.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1–L2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Mainly from internal oblique muscle and adjacent inguinal ligament.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Forms loops around the spermatic cord and testis, blending with coverings around the cord.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectum

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stores faeces before defecation.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Begins at the rectosigmoid junction around S3 and follows the sacral curve to the anorectal junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the male, lies posterior to the bladder, seminal vesicles and prostate.

cards.question: Blood supply
cards.answer: Superior rectal artery with contributions from middle and inferior rectal arteries.

cards.question: Lymphatic drainage
cards.answer: Upper rectum drains mainly toward pararectal and inferior mesenteric nodes; lower rectum also drains to internal iliac nodes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Bifurcation of the abdominal aorta, usually at L4.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs inferolaterally toward the sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Terminates as the external and internal iliac arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb through its terminal branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Common iliac veins lie mainly posterior; the ureter crosses near the iliac bifurcation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac vein

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Union of the external and internal iliac veins.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends toward the right side of L5 where the right and left common iliac veins unite.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Right and left common iliac veins form the inferior vena cava.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Common iliac arteries lie anterior; the right common iliac artery crosses anterior to the left common iliac vein.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Peritoneum

cards.question: Definition
cards.answer: Serous membrane lining the abdominopelvic cavity and covering intraperitoneal viscera.

cards.question: Layers
cards.answer: Parietal peritoneum lines the body wall; visceral peritoneum covers organs.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: In the male pelvis, reflects from the bladder onto the rectum to form the rectovesical pouch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parietal peritoneum has somatic innervation and is pain-sensitive; visceral peritoneum has autonomic visceral afferent innervation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inguinal ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle; formed by the rolled inferior border of the external oblique aponeurosis.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the floor of the inguinal canal and a key boundary between abdomen and thigh.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Deep to it pass iliopsoas and femoral nerve through the muscular lacuna and femoral vessels through the vascular lacuna.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important landmark for distinguishing inguinal from femoral hernias.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pectineal part of the inguinal ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends medially/posteriorly toward the pecten pubis in the medial inguinal region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Related to the medial side of the femoral ring and pectineal fascia.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contributes to reinforcement of the medial subinguinal region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Femoral canal

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Medial compartment of the femoral sheath, medial to the femoral vein.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Loose connective tissue, lymphatics and the deep inguinal lymph node.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Allows expansion of the femoral vein and provides a lymphatic passage.

cards.question: Boundaries
cards.answer: At the femoral ring: inguinal ligament anteriorly, pectineal ligament posteriorly, lacunar ligament medially and femoral vein laterally.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Site of femoral hernias, which have a relatively high risk of strangulation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vascular lacuna

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Subinguinal space medial to the iliopectineal arch.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Femoral artery, femoral vein and femoral canal/lymphatics.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Separated from the muscular lacuna by the iliopectineal arch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Interfoveolar ligament

cards.question: Also called
cards.answer: Hesselbach’s ligament.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Thickening of transversalis fascia near the medial side of the deep inguinal ring.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Related to the inferior epigastric vessels and posterior wall of the inguinal region.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contributes to reinforcement of the posterior inguinal wall around the deep ring.
